title: Why Our Galaxy’s Black Hole Hasn’t Swallowed Us
description:
A giant black hole lives at the center of the Milky Way. Why are we still here? An equal-mass thought experiment reveals why black holes are not cosmic vacuum cleaners.

Original motion graphics and synthetic English narration. Diagrams are schematic and not to scale.

Sources: NASA
https://science.nasa.gov/solar-system/10-questions-you-might-have-about-black-holes/
https://www.nasa.gov/image-article/supermassive-black-hole-sagittarius/

scenes.title: Why hasn’t it swallowed us?
scenes.image_credit: Original schematic illustration, Keou Production. NASA facts; not to scale.
scenes.voice: There is a giant black hole at the center of our galaxy. So why hasn't it swallowed us?

scenes.title: A heavyweight in the dark.
scenes.unit: times the mass of our Sun
scenes.voice: It packs roughly four million times the mass of our Sun. But mass alone does not tell the whole story.

scenes.title: Gravity follows rules.
scenes.quote: A black hole is no cosmic vacuum cleaner.
scenes.voice: Black holes do not magically suck everything in. From far away, their gravity depends on mass and distance.

scenes.title: New object. Same orbit.
scenes.image_credit: Original schematic illustration, Keou Production. Equal-mass thought experiment from NASA; not to scale.
scenes.voice: Imagine replacing the Sun with a black hole of exactly the same mass. Earth would keep its orbit.

scenes.title: The orbit stays. The light goes.
scenes.voice: We would lose sunlight, which would be disastrous for life. But we would not suddenly spiral into the center.

scenes.title: We are a long way out.
scenes.voice: Our galaxy's central black hole is about twenty six thousand light years away. It is not about to swallow Earth.

scenes.title: More than a scary name.
scenes.voice: To understand an orbit, ask about mass, distance, and motion. The words black hole are not enough.

scenes.title: What happens at the edge?
scenes.voice: The real mystery begins much closer. What would happen if you crossed the point of no return?
